answer.reason: Different business model: Wendy’s serves made-to-order restaurant meals through drive-thru and delivery and recruits franchise owners. Tootsie manufactures packaged candy, chocolate and gum sold through retail venues. Broad consumer appeal does not establish a shared buyer or dining occasion.
answer.missing_evidence: Tootsie’s direct purchasing customers are not specified, but the passages sufficiently establish distinct offerings and business models.

citations.text: Tootsie’s brands include some of the most familiar candy names: Tootsie Roll, Tootsie Pop, Charms Blow Pop, DOTS, Andes Mints, Sugar Daddy, Charleston Chew, Dubble Bubble, Razzles, Caramel Apple Pop, Junior Mints, Cella’s Chocolate-Covered Cherries, and Nik-L-Nip. They’re sold in a wide variety of venues, including supermarkets, warehouse and membership stores, vending machines, dollar stores, drug stores, and convenience stores.

citations.label: C:P2.8
citations.text: As America’s favorite candy company, satisfying America’s sweet tooth requires an extraordinary collective effort. Tootsie rises impressively to the challenge, producing millions of pieces of candy every day from its North American plants. Applying state-of-the-art production technology and exacting quality control checks, Tootsie ensures that every piece of gum, candy, and chocolate that rolls off of its production lines is of the highest, most consistent quality—every time.

citations.label: C:P2.11
citations.text: Have you ever been curious how Tootsie Roll Industries gets the Tootsie Roll into the center of the Tootsie Pop, how DOTS are made, or what color Crows are? Get a first-hand look at how products like Tootsie Rolls, Tootsie Pops, and more are manufactured and packaged. Listen as Mrs. Ellen Gordon and Mr. Melvin Gordon discuss the history of Tootsie Roll Industries, their experience with America’s candy favorites, and just how many licks it takes to get to the center of a Tootsie Roll Tootsie Pop!
